big: Rohan earns a salary every month and gets a bonus once a year. He wants to invest, but he is not sure how to begin, or what to do with each kind of money.

lines: What do I need before I can buy my first fund?
Three things: a one-time KYC, a fund that suits your goal, and a way to pay. Then comes the best part, making it a habit.

intro: Do these once and you can invest in any fund.
rows: One-time identity check with PAN and address proof
Your account number with a fund house
The person who can claim your units
Monthly habit, or one bigger amount
note: Add a nominee at the start. It saves your family time and paperwork later.

alt: Six monthly instalments of ₹5,000 buying different numbers of units as the price changes
caps: Month 1. The unit price is ₹20, so ₹5,000 buys 250 units.
The price slips to ₹19, so the same money buys more units.
At ₹18 it buys the most. Nobody had to guess the right day.
The price rises again. Fewer units, but the earlier ones are worth more.
A SIP makes investing a habit. It does not promise a profit.

q: Rohan skips KYC because 'I will do it when I find the right fund'. What is the problem?
opts: None, since KYC is only needed when he sells the units he holds later
He needs a fresh KYC for every new fund he buys from any fund house
KYC is only for investments above ₹10 lakh in a single year
He cannot invest until the one-time KYC is done, so he should do it first
why: KYC is needed before investing, not only when selling. Skipping it means he cannot start.
KYC is done once and works across funds. It is not repeated for each fund bought.
KYC is required for investing in mutual funds whatever the amount. There is no size threshold.
KYC is a one-time check. Once it is done, he can invest in funds across fund houses.

q: Rohan gets his ₹60,000 bonus in March. His goal is a car down payment in four years. What is a sound approach?
opts: Put it all into the highest-risk fund to grow it fast before the car is due
A fund whose risk fits a four-year goal, invested as a lump sum or in a few parts
Spend it, since a one-time bonus is too small to be worth investing at all
Wait for the market to look cheap before investing, however long that takes
why: High risk near a four-year goal can mean a fall just before the money is needed.
Match the fund to a four-year goal, then invest the lump sum at once or in a few steps.
A bonus can be invested. Small amounts add up when they are put to work for a goal.
Waiting for a cheap-looking market is guesswork, and it can mean never starting.

q: Meena's SIP buys 250 units at ₹20 and 263 units at ₹19. What does this show?
opts: A fixed amount buys more units when the price is lower, fewer when higher
The SIP gives bonus units whenever the price happens to drop
The fund house cuts the unit price for SIP investors every month
The SIP is certain to make a profit because it collects extra units
why: A fixed amount means lower prices buy more units and higher prices buy fewer.
The extra units are bought with the same money at a lower price, not given by anyone.
The price is set by the fund's holdings, not adjusted for SIP investors.
More units do not guarantee a profit if the price keeps falling. A SIP is a method, not a promise.

q: A father wants his daughter to be able to claim his investments quickly if something happens to him. What should he have done?
opts: Keep a written note with his passwords in a drawer at home for her
Invest only in her name, whatever his own goals may be
Name her as nominee in each folio, so she can claim with less paperwork
Nothing, because units are always claimed by the fund house
why: A note with passwords is risky and does not give a legal route to claim the units.
Investing only in her name ignores his own goals and does not fit every situation.
A nominee named in the folio can claim the units with far less paperwork for the family.
Units belong to the holder and his heirs, not to the fund house. A nominee smooths the claim.

pts: Complete KYC once and you can invest in any fund.
A SIP turns investing into a monthly habit. It does not promise a profit.
Name a nominee so your family can claim without a long process.
